works.version: Physics Letters B 695, pp.174–180 (2011), publisher PDF
scope: PDF1–2 introduction, HFB/QPM and first 2+ comparison
PDF3–5 strength response and proton/neutron radial densities
PDF6–7 conclusions, diffusivity discussion and references
checks: The first page and figure captions establish 104–134Sn as the target chain. The old 58–78Ni widths/strengths do not belong to the original source.
PDF2 Fig. 1 compares calculations with cited first-2+ data; PDF3 Figs. 2–3 give predicted components and summed strengths.
PDF5 Fig. 5 and PDF6 Eqs. 3.4–3.5 model different radial structures and surface diffusivity. The model treats 132Sn as a special shell-closure case.
works.gap: PQR identification depends on the calculated transition-density and spectral evidence. The source does not measure nickel intensities or continuum damping widths.
works.lineage: Theory with prior tin spectroscopy as a comparison. The former nickel parametrization remains an independent historical toy calculation.

scope: PDF1–4 Compton response and ion-trap experiment
PDF5–7 event reconstruction, angular measurement and simulation
PDF8–10 likelihood and modulation, controls and conclusions
checks: PDF3 Fig. 2 establishes the segmented Si/CdTe architecture and geometric angles. Data are from atomic Kr recombination x rays around 75.5 keV.
PDF7–8 Figs. 7–9: an independent 133Ba control gives residual instrument modulation Q near 0.010.
PDF8–10 Eqs. 5–8, Figs. 12–15: Pi=0.962(8 stat)(15 sys) is the main likelihood result. The modulation-curve cross-check reuses the same Kr events.
works.gap: Energy ordering, acceptance and residual modulation depend on detector/energy/cuts. No benchmark for physical nuclear line polarization at a different energy is provided by this measurement.
works.lineage: One Tokyo EBIT experimental sample; Ba response control is a separately measured calibration. Archived version precedes the published layout.
